title: AK SDLC skill map
description: Read left to right, then down. This is the PR implementation route; select only the methods the task needs. Focused skills also work directly without starting SDLC.
subtitle: Follow the stages, choose the method, or find a skill for the task in front of you.

phases.title: Understand
phases.summary: Clarify the outcome and inspect the evidence.

phases.title: Shape
phases.summary: Agree on the contract, design and reviewable slices.

phases.title: Build & prove
phases.summary: Implement small slices and verify the integrated candidate.

phases.title: Review & deliver
phases.summary: Resolve findings and stop at the authorized endpoint.

steps.label: Coordinator selects the route

stages.title: Intent
stages.summary: Resolve consequential unknowns before committing to a plan.

steps.label: Choose an interview: lightweight OR durable docs

stages.title: Investigation
stages.summary: Trace existing behavior; reproduce uncertain failures.
stages.handoff: Source-backed facts, reproduction and open questions.

steps.label: Understand unfamiliar code
For a difficult defect, diagnose the cause

stages.title: Specification
stages.summary: Synthesize the agreed intent and investigation.

steps.label: Create or update the specification

stages.title: Design
stages.summary: Settle interfaces, ownership and consequential tradeoffs.
stages.handoff: Selected design, alternatives and supporting evidence.

steps.label: Lead the design
For competing designs: compare providers; return to architect
When a diagram clarifies the design

stages.title: Plan
stages.summary: Sequence thin, verifiable slices and appropriate PR boundaries.

steps.label: Decompose the agreed scope
Keep one execution notebook
If tickets or drafts are requested

stages.title: Test design
stages.summary: Identify observable behavior and how to prove it.
stages.gate: Non-executable changes may use alternative evidence
stages.handoff: Focused test plan or justified alternative checks.

steps.label: Use the collection’s single test-first method

stages.title: Build
stages.summary: Implement and check each slice, then integrate.
stages.gate: Parallel work requires independent, authorized slices
stages.handoff: Changes and evidence from the combined candidate.

steps.label: Run the test-first loop
If independent slices can run in parallel

stages.title: Self-verification
stages.summary: Exercise the actual integrated candidate and affected scenarios.
stages.handoff: Candidate-bound checks, coverage and explicit gaps.

steps.label: For this repository: run the project-local checks
When screenshot/PDF documentation applies

stages.title: PR review
stages.summary: Prepare a reviewable candidate, then review it independently.

steps.label: Author prepares the PR when needed
SDLC assigns reviewers; each applies this method once

stages.title: Correction
stages.summary: Fix confirmed findings and renew affected verification and review.

steps.label: If the cause is uncertain, diagnose first
Fix behavior through the same test-first loop

stages.title: Merge
stages.summary: Integrate only after the required gates and explicit merge authority.
stages.gate: Only for an authorized main endpoint

steps.label: Coordinator checks authority and integrates

stages.title: Completion
stages.summary: Report the result, evidence, limits and remaining handoff.

steps.label: Coordinator closes the task

excluded_stages.reason: Not a separate stage on the current PR implementation route. It remains in the state model for explicitly requested local, plan-only or review-only lifecycle runs.

anytime.title: Clarify & understand
anytime.description: Revisit an assumption or unfamiliar area at any point.

anytime.title: Organize & communicate
anytime.description: Maintain context and produce the record the task actually needs.

anytime.title: Create & maintain verification
anytime.description: Fill a missing repeatable check or repair known drift within the current stage.

anytime.title: Policies & tool connections
anytime.description: Consult applicable policies and connection prerequisites; selecting a card installs nothing.

anytime.title: Account sources and runtime
anytime.description: Source preparation and diagnostics only; this map installs nothing.

anytime.title: Self-improvement and eval
anytime.description: A separate improvement cycle, not extra mandatory PR stages: 1 Observe -> 2 Reproduce -> 3 Candidate -> 4 Eval -> 5 Review -> 6 Deploy -> Observe again. Synthetic storage, opt-in Claude/Codex collection, offline evaluation accounting and the installer exist; live model comparison and automatic promotion remain planned. Native trust and platform gaps are explicit. Available means the source guide exists, not that its runtime is implemented.

triggers.grill-me: A consequential idea or requirement is still ambiguous; sharpen it through an interview without creating domain documents.
triggers.grill-with-docs: The interview also needs durable domain terms or architectural decisions in a glossary and ADRs.
triggers.grilling: You want to stress-test a plan or decision through focused questions; it is also the interview method used by the two grill wrappers.
triggers.domain-modeling: Terminology is inconsistent, or a glossary or architectural decision needs to be recorded or refined.
triggers.how: You need a source-backed explanation of unfamiliar execution flow, ownership or subsystem boundaries before changing code.
triggers.diagnosing-bugs: A difficult or intermittent failure has an uncertain cause; reproduce it and test hypotheses before fixing it.
triggers.planning-with-files: Research or execution spans many steps or tool calls and needs one persistent task notebook.
triggers.archify: An architecture, workflow or interaction is easier to understand as an explorable, validated diagram.
triggers.writing-for-agents: The artifact you are authoring or reviewing is an agent skill, policy or instruction.
triggers.issue-writing: You are authorized to draft, create or rewrite an issue body with clear scope and verifiable acceptance criteria.
triggers.screenshot-manual: Users need instructions demonstrated with real product screenshots and a rendered, visually checked PDF.
triggers.create-verification-skill: A real project lacks repeatable user-facing verification; establish its verifier and feature recipes.
triggers.maintain-verification-skill: Existing verification recipes may have drifted and a scoped audit or repair has been requested.
triggers.repository-verifier: You changed this repository’s catalog UI or map generation and need its actual browser and freshness checks.
triggers.repository-feature-map: You need to identify the affected repository user journey and find its verification recipe.
triggers.policy-architecture: Code is hard for agents to find, understand or verify, or you are designing a new project boundary.
triggers.policy-behavioral-tests: You are designing tests and need to choose observable behavior instead of implementation details.
triggers.policy-evidence: You are about to claim completion or correctness and need evidence tied to the actual candidate.
triggers.policy-security: Work touches public source, credentials, access boundaries or externally supplied material.
triggers.policy-logging: You add or review logs, choose diagnostic levels, structure events or remove temporary debug probes.
triggers.policy-issue-workflow: Work is tracked by an issue and needs a progress update, decision, blocker, handoff or closure record.
triggers.policy-visual-documentation: A change needs a diagram or screenshot manual and you must establish source and verification requirements.
triggers.policy-pr-workflow: You are splitting work into reviewable PRs, preparing the review context or coordinating dependent PRs.
triggers.mcp-context7: A task needs current library documentation; inspect the connection template and prerequisites before opting in.
triggers.mcp-github: Authorized work needs GitHub issue or PR access through MCP; inspect credential and permission requirements first.
triggers.mcp-playwright: A task needs browser interaction or screenshots through MCP; inspect the isolated browser setup first.
triggers.tool-registry: You need to select or verify an external CLI, diagram, PDF or MCP dependency.
triggers.policy-communication: Writing a reply, issue, PR, document or UI copy.
triggers.policy-execution: Starting multi-stage work, handing off, or resuming an existing task.
triggers.account-source: Setting up another host, updating the shared bundle, removing it or reviewing ownership conflicts.
triggers.planning-hooks: Preparing or verifying lifecycle integration for planning-with-files.
triggers.reviewer-runtime: A review resumes after correction or a launcher cannot represent a setting.
triggers.observation-store: Step 1: opt in one approved client/project, inspect callback/platform limits, or verify bounded delivery snapshots and measured collector capacity.
triggers.improvement-case: An observed failure needs a reproducible case before changing a skill, policy or MCP configuration. Planned: turn bounded observations and feedback into a synthetic reproducible case.
triggers.improvement-candidate: A reviewed reproduction supports a concrete hypothesis about a skill, policy or MCP change. Manual method available; loop orchestration planned: form one minimal, reviewable source candidate.
triggers.improvement-eval: Offline accounting is available for supplied synthetic completions; a live runner and independent holdout qualification remain planned.
triggers.improvement-review: A comparison proposes changing the source used by future account tasks. Existing review methods support a planned promotion gate for skill improvements.
triggers.improvement-deploy: An accepted committed candidate is authorized for account deployment. Existing installer available; automatic eval-to-deployment integration remains planned.
triggers.account-doctor: After setup or upgrades: diagnose files, check native discovery/trust, then optionally run a real low-cost model. Add Paseo only when selected. Supports setup qualification before eval and after deployment; does not establish comparative improvement.
triggers.native-isolation: Before live evaluation, verify native discovery, mock transport and denied access in a restricted container.
